audit_findings.title: Forecast owner-earnings growth and the frozen share denominator may describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed capital plan is $8.7 billion for 2026-2030, and more than half of $3.495 billion planned for 2027-2028 requires external financing
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental interest reduces equity-level OE, while equity issuance increases the per-share denominator; either can make aggregate OE growth exceed OE-per-share growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The ability to finance our future construction programs, as well as our acquisition activities, depends on our ability to attract the necessary external debt and equity financing and maintain internally-generated funds.
audit_findings.explanation: The financing exposure is demonstrated: the company expects substantial external financing, issued 7.671350 million ATM shares in 2025, and retains approximately $648 million of ATM capacity. The error itself remains unresolved because the record does not show whether the 6%-8% growth paths already include future interest and dilution. Given the financing scale and the valuation's dependence on sustained growth, the mismatch is reasonably capable of materially overstating per-share value.
audit_findings.action: Produce a year-by-year capital and financing schedule showing internally generated funds, new debt, interest expense, equity issuance and diluted shares, then rerun every scenario as OE per share.

audit_findings.title: Customer regulatory liabilities may be an unmodeled claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed regulatory liabilities are $714.487 million versus regulatory assets of $2,109.448 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Refunds, bill credits and liability amortization can reduce future OE, while recovery and amortization of regulatory assets can increase it; these are forecast-flow effects rather than an automatic bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Regulatory assets represent costs that are probable to be fully recovered from customers in future rates while regulatory liabilities represent amounts that are expected to be refunded to customers in future rates or amounts recovered from customers in advance of incurring the costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The balances are demonstrated and large: regulatory liabilities equal approximately 120% of the $595.9 million anchor and 7.2% of base equity value. However, the record does not provide the timing, earnings treatment or offsetting asset recoveries needed to translate the balance-sheet amounts into OE. It therefore may affect value materially, but neither a net adverse claim nor its materiality is established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each material regulatory asset and liability to governing rate orders, refund or recovery schedules and forecast revenue or expense effects, then rerun the DCF using the net annual OE impacts.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring tax-related benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.575 million benefit; if fully retained and perpetuated, computed value overstatement is approximately $0.94 per share bear, $1.31 base and $1.46 bull
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax benefit in anchor OE is compounded through forecast growth and terminal value; an unsustainable terminal tax assumption similarly overstates future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In the first quarter of 2025, based on the rate order received by Aqua Pennsylvania, the Company released $ 22,575 of income tax reserve regulatory liability, while the remaining the tax benefit of $ 4,874 will be refunded to customers through base rates over a two-year period.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $22.575 million release benefited 2025 and did not recur in the first half of 2026. It does not demonstrate that the valuation worksheet retained the item. The specific amount is 3.8% of anchor OE and, by itself, would not reverse the conclusion that even bull value of $38.51 is below the $41.70 price. Materiality remains uncertain because the sustainable tax burden behind the 0.6% effective rate has not been established and could exceed this discrete item.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $595.9 million anchor to filed net income, show any subtraction of the $22.575 million release and related customer refunds, establish a sustainable tax schedule for repair deductions and regulatory sharing, and rerun all scenarios if either treatment is absent.

audit_findings.title: Equity AFUDC may be counted as cash owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.278 million, equal to 3.1% of anchor OE; full recurring removal would reduce computed base value by approximately $1.06 per share and bull value by approximately $1.18 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If not removed from net-income-based OE, noncash equity AFUDC enters the anchor and is capitalized through forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of AFUDC related to equity was $18,278 in 2025 and $13,938 in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $18.278 million of equity AFUDC but does not establish that the OE worksheet failed to subtract it. Even the conservative test of removing the entire amount from recurring OE leaves computed bull value near $37.33 per share, still about $4.37 below the $41.70 market price. The issue therefore does not change the present valuation conclusion, although worksheet treatment should still be verified.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE reconciliation for an explicit equity-AFUDC subtraction and confirm subsequent rate recovery is counted only when earned; correct the worksheet if absent, without otherwise changing assumptions.

audit_findings.title: PFAS remediation creates a future recurring expense stream not demonstrated in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $22.5 million of annual operating expense at the filed minimum $450 million installed-capital estimate; net burden after rate recovery and settlements is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Testing, treatment and disposal expenses reduce future OE as facilities enter service, subject to the timing and extent of rate recovery and settlement offsets.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, the Company estimates annual operating expenses of approximately five percent of the installed capital expenditures, in today’s dollars, related to testing, treatment, and disposal.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a disclosed future cost ramp rather than a demonstrated error in 2025 OE. Five percent of at least $450 million implies approximately $22.5 million annually, or 3.8% of anchor OE, before recovery. Regulatory recovery has historically been available, and PFAS settlement proceeds are being assigned regulatory treatment, so the shareholder-level burden and timing cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Track installed PFAS capital, commissioned sites, actual operating costs, settlement allocations and rate orders; incorporate the unrecovered annual cost and regulatory lag in the forecast as those amounts become determinable.

audit_findings.title: Merger advisory fees are a specific contingent claim missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $35 million remaining after $25 million incurred through June 30, 2026, equal to approximately $0.12 per share; the full $60 million fee equals approximately $0.21 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid merger fee is a one-time cash deduction from equity value or future OE and should not be capitalized as a recurring operating expense.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 25, 2025, the Company entered into an agreement with a financial advisor (“Advisor”) for services to be rendered in connection with the consummation of a Merger with American Water, pursuant to which the Company will pay the Advisor a fee of $ 60,000 (“Transaction Fee”) upon the achievement of certain milestones.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves much of the amount: $12 million was incurred by year-end 2025 and another $13 million during the first half of 2026, leaving at most $35 million of the stated transaction fee. A full remaining bridge deduction is approximately $0.12 per share, far below the $7.19 gap between base value and market price and the $17.54 gap between the buy-below price and market price. It cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the accrued liability and remaining milestone terms at the next filing, then deduct only the unpaid expected amount once—either through forecast OE or the bridge—to avoid double counting.
